headline: Loan growth and a Visa gain power a strong quarter
summary_short: BOK Financial earned $2.92 diluted EPS in Q2 FY2026, up from $2.58 in Q1 and $2.19 a year ago, as loans grew a record $896 million to $27.1 billion and net interest margin held at 2.91%.
summary_long: Net interest income rose $9.3 million to $351.8 million as margin held at 2.91%, benefiting from repricing of fixed-rate assets and deposits, partly offset by cash margin posted for energy clients. Fee income fell $7.8 million on lower trading activity, though fiduciary and asset-management revenue hit a record. A $30.9 million pre-tax Visa B gain and a $4.6 million AFS repositioning loss lifted reported net income to $176.5 million ($2.92/share); adjusted net income was $156.5 million ($2.59/share), up from $155.8 million ($2.58/share) in Q1. Loans grew a record $896 million to $27.1 billion; deposits rose $1.2 billion to $39.9 billion. CET1 improved to 12.89% from 12.61%; net charge-offs were 0.01% of loans, no provision required. No new guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Pretax income rose q/q as net interest income grew $9.3 million and other gains swung to a $42.4 million net gain (mainly the Visa B share exchange), partially offset by $7.5 million higher operating expense.

Net income included a $30.9 million pre-tax Visa B share-exchange gain and a $4.6 million available-for-sale portfolio repositioning loss; excluding both, adjusted net income was $156.5 million versus $155.8 million in Q1.
GAAP EPS benefited from the same Visa gain and AFS loss as net income; adjusted EPS was $2.59, up modestly from $2.58 in the prior quarter, a cleaner q/q comparison.

Derived from net income of $176.5 million less common dividends of roughly $38.1 million and a nominal $0.3 million buyback, partly offset by a wider unrealized AFS-securities loss within accumulated other comprehensive loss.

Share count was roughly flat q/q — only 2,519 shares were repurchased this quarter versus 2.6 million in Q4 2025 and 663,298 a year ago, so the y/y decline reflects prior-period buybacks, not this quarter.

CEO Stacy Kymes cited the highest quarterly loan production in company history, loans up nearly $900 million in the quarter and 11.5% y/y, stable margins, and record Fiduciary and Asset Management revenue.
